title: Slow-Smoked Beef Brisket with Salt and Pepper Bark
summary: A whole brisket with a simple salt and pepper rub is smoked low and slow, wrapped to finish until butter-soft, then rested and sliced with quick cucumber pickles and raw onion.
equipment: smoker or kettle barbecue (at least 57 cm) set up for indirect cooking
oven thermometer or the smoker gauge
pink butcher paper or heavy foil
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray
insulated cool box and old towels

ingredients.item: whole beef brisket (point and flat), fat trimmed to 5 mm
fine sea salt or table salt
oak or hickory wood chunks (about 8 cm)
medium white onions, thinly sliced, to serve

steps.title: Apply the rub
steps.text: Pat the brisket dry, mix the salt and pepper and press it all over the meat. Ideally the night before, refrigerate it uncovered on a rack over the tray for 8-24 h, though you can cook straight away. Resting uncovered dries the surface, which helps the bark form.

steps.title: Set up the cooker
steps.text: Heat the smoker or kettle for indirect cooking to 110-120°C and add 2-3 wood chunks to the coals. On a kettle, bank the coals to one side with a tray of water under the cooking area. The water steadies the temperature and keeps the air moist.

steps.title: Smoke low and slow
steps.text: Place the brisket fat side up over the indirect zone with the thicker point towards the heat, and insert the leave-in probe into the thickest part of the flat. Close the lid and hold the cooker at 110-120°C, adding charcoal and the last wood chunks as needed. Smoke for 6-8 h, until the bark is dark and set and the probe reads about 75°C.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.text: Wrap the brisket tightly in 2 layers of butcher paper or foil, fat side up, and return it to the cooker or a 120°C (fan 100°C) oven. Cook for 2-4 h more, until the probe reads 93-95°C and slides in like soft butter in several places. Wrapping pushes it past the stage where evaporation slows the cooking, while the long heat melts the collagen.

steps.title: Rest in a cool box
steps.text: Wrap the parcel in towels, place it in the cool box and rest for 1-2 h; it stays well above 63°C. Serve within 4 h of finishing, or chill it. Resting lets the juices redistribute so they stay in the meat when you slice.

steps.title: Quick-pickle
steps.text: During the rest, warm the cider vinegar and sugar until dissolved, then pour over the cucumber and jalapeño and leave for 30 min. Drain before serving; the sharp pickles cut through the rich beef.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Separate the flat from the point. Slice the flat across the grain about 6 mm thick, then turn the point 90° and slice it across its own grain a little thicker. Spoon over the juices from the paper and serve with sliced onion and the pickles.

tips: A common mistake is pulling the brisket by time alone; it is ready when the probe slides in like soft butter at 93-95°C in several spots.
Keep the cooker temperature steady at 110-120°C and avoid lifting the lid too often, which lets heat and smoke escape.
Slice against the grain of each muscle, as the flat and point run in different directions.
Use only a few wood chunks; too much smoke turns the bark bitter.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate in their juices for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat covered with a splash of the juices until piping hot (74°C).
